text:
tayla: Heads up — Acme reporting recurring p95 token latency spikes + intermittent 429s on their eu2 dedicated pool since ~03:20 UTC. Seeing 'slice busy' and increased kv-cache miss rates in our logs. @pradeep @noah can you take a look?

pradeep: Got it. Do we have tenant id / pool / example request ids and node ids to trace?

tayla: Tenant: acme-corp, pool: eu2-dedicated-7. Example request: req=0e3f2a, node=gpu-03-1. Pasted tail of runtime log:```
[03:21:12] request 0e3f2a -> 429 SliceBusy: MIG slice busy, retry after 120ms
[03:21:12] kvcache: miss (prefix 0x7f), fallback to full context
[03:21:13] request 0e3f2a -> succeeded after retry, token_latency=780ms
[03:21:30] p95 token latency 1.1s (baseline 220ms)
```

mig-watch-bot: ALERT: MIG_SIBLING_SATURATION detected on node gpu-03-1. sm_util spikes to 98% for 18s, concurrent tenants on node: 4. Suggested: check fractional packing / placement.

noah: SM saturation definitely smells like noisy neighbor. This is a dedicated pool but note: dedicated != single-host isolation by default. Can someone paste `nvidia-smi mig -li` and current packing?

pradeep: Pulled node config and recent scheduler actions. `nvidia-smi mig -li` excerpt:```
GPU 0:
  InstanceProfileId: 1g.5gb  Count: 1
  InstanceProfileId: 2g.10gb Count: 2
GPU 1:...
```
acme-corp's tasks pinned to a 2g.10gb slice but scheduler placed a bursty analytics tenant on neighboring 2g.10gb and two small 1g.5gb tenants on same host — fractional packing + short-lived batch bursts coincide with the spike times.

tayla: Customer says the spikes align with their nightly batch window at 03:15 UTC. They assumed dedicated pool would avoid that kind of interference. They purchased reserved capacity but not a single-tenant host. They want a mitigation ASAP.

pradeep: Immediate mitigations I recommend: (1) live-migrate acme-corp workloads to a node with empty MIG slices in same AZ, (2) temporarily bump their autoscale min slots and set placement override = node_isolation, (3) throttle the noisy tenant if it's in our pool and it's violating burst policy. I'll start the migration and open an eviction.

noah: Before migration, take a perf snapshot for post-mortem: `perf record` or nvprof for a sample window. Also capture `nvml` metrics for sm_util, l2, memory bw around the event.

pradeep: Initiating eviction/drain for acme-corp from gpu-03-1 now. Command: `redwoodctl pools evict --pool eu2-dedicated-7 --node gpu-03-1 --tenant acme-corp`. Eviction ID ev-66012. ETA ~4m.

mig-watch-bot: ACTION: Eviction started (ev-66012). Monitoring telemetry for migration window.

tayla: Messaging customer with ETA and applying a 10% credit for the SLA disruption. cc @lee for account outreach. :thumbsup:

lee: Thanks — I'll send the advisory and offer options: (A) reserve a whole host for them (single-tenant), (B) update placement policy for stricter isolation, or (C) schedule the nightly batch off-peak.

pradeep: Post-mortem action items I propose: - auto-detect fractional packing when tenant SLA is above threshold and surface a placement warning; - new placement rule: avoid mixing 1g/2g slices with high-SLA tenants on same host; - add KV-cache eviction telemetry to surface prefix thrash. Assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

noah: After migration p95 dropped back to baseline (~230ms). Will monitor for 30m. Marking triage as resolved -> pending follow-up for placement policy change.

tayla: :white_check_mark: Migration succeeded, customer stable. Closing thread after 30m stable window.
